children: Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company, SpaceX (SPCX, Financials), is about to run a test that might validate several of its grandest dreams at once. Starship's 14th trip is set for Sept. 22 and this one is different.
For the first time, SpaceX will put its Starship spacecraft into orbit around Earth and deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites.
Ultimately, those satellites could provide more than 100 times the bandwidth of SpaceX's existing constellation, Musk says. But Wall Street is looking past Starlink.
Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas recently kept a $300 price estimate, saying the value didn't fully represent SpaceX's AI and orbital-computing possibilities.
Bernstein analyst Douglas Harned has a $248 target and thinks reusable Starship launches are needed to enable orbiting data centers. That makes Sept. 22 more than just another rocket launch.

As SpaceX builds its future, an increasing amount of that future is built around businesses that need Starship to fly often and affordably, from next-gen Starlink satellites to computer infrastructure in orbit.
That model alone will not demonstrate the first orbital attempt. But it could reveal if one of the most important elements is coming closer to reality.

title: SpaceX stock rises as Starship prepares for historic orbital test
